## About
SA Card House is a members' poker room in San Antonio for players of every level, from people learning the game to seasoned regulars. We run cash games with a range of betting limits and host poker tournaments, including Omaha, on a regular schedule.
We recently moved into a bigger, renovated space in the old Luby's building, with room to spread out, large screen TVs for the game or a WSOP broadcast, and Foster’s Bar and Grill for food and drinks while you play.
Safety comes first here. We have security staff on site and cameras throughout the building, and the doors are open every day, all day and all night.

## Services
- Cash games: Cash games with a variety of betting limits. Become a member, buy chips and find a seat.
- Tournaments: Poker tournaments held on a regular schedule.
- Initial membership: A one-time membership to start playing at SA Card House. ($20)
- Daily access ($5)
- Monthly access ($50)
- Bar and kitchen: An on-site bar and kitchen, so you can order food and drinks without leaving the game.

## FAQ
Q: Do I need to be a member to play?
A: Yes. To play cash games you first become a member, then purchase chips.

Q: When are you open?
A: We are open 24 hours a day, every day.

Q: Is there a discount for military or first responders?
A: Yes, we offer a military and first responder discount. Ask the staff for details.

Q: I'm new to poker. Is this a good place to start?
A: Yes. Our room is set up for players of every skill level, from beginners to seasoned pros.

## What customers say
- "High Action! It might be called SA Card House, but I refer to it as Action City in my mind. And this isn't your standard kind of poker action.

First off, Texas poker plays differently than anywhere else. It’s much more action-based and ego-driven. If you're wondering what this means, standard casino rooms usually feature a mix of tight-aggressive players who only strike when they have a mathematical edge. You don't get that here. Players are incredibly loose and love putting chips in the middle.

If you want to see massive pots sitting in a big pile in the middle of the felt, go straight to SA Card House. Based on my experiences here, the cash games have a unique style and I recommend folding a few orbits to adapt. You will see tons of multi-way pots and deep-stacked players willing to call down with draws.

For tournaments, the play is highly beatable because many players treat them like wild cash games. I managed a 2nd place finish and cashed another during my visit. And the tournaments are very well run, which puts your mind at ease and allows you to play your A game.

As for the aesthetics and professionalism of the room, they are both right on the money. The space is super clean, the dealers are top-tier, and the players are welcoming.

An added bonus is that the parking lot is elevated, incredibly well-lit, and feels exceptionally secure when you walk to your car at night.

To leave a balanced review, I always try to include a critique. The room had a shift in their kitchen staff right around my visit, so I hope they maintain consistency with their food menu moving forward, as a stable kitchen really rounds out a great poker room.

Overall, if the primary things you are seeking are beatable games, high action, and a clean environment where you feel safe walking to your vehicle, this spot is easily at the top of the board. Definitely recommended." (Tyler Nals, 5/5)
- "By far the best club in the city.  Not only is the action great at the tables, but the food at Foster’s is amazing as well.  From players to staff, the people here are like family gathering at family reunion. Fun, laughs and friendships.  Tournaments are great and they have adequate rules structure unlike other local houses.  SACH does a great job with floor management and fair floor calls." (Izzy Villalobos, 5/5)

I highly recommend getting a few drinks while sitting at the table." (Richard, 5/5)
- ""Had an amazing time playing in The Big Blind's tournament. Structure was fair, pace was solid, and the staff kept everything running smooth and honest. New to tournaments? You'll be welcomed, not eaten alive. If you're serious about the game, this is where you  play." (ISAAC DAY, 5/5)
